problem.title: Container With Most Water
problem.statement: You have several walls of different heights. Choose two walls that, when placed facing each other, can hold the most water. Return the maximum water volume.
problem.hint: Water volume = distance between walls x height of the shorter wall. If you move the taller wall, can the volume increase? Think about: which wall should you move?
problem.walkthrough:
Example wall heights: [1, 8, 6, 2, 5, 4, 8, 3, 7].

Start at the widest apart: left=1, right=7. Volume = min(1,7) x 8 = 8.
Move left (shorter one) to 8. Volume = min(8,7) x 7 = 49. Bigger!
Move right to 3. Volume = min(8,3) x 6 = 18. Smaller.
...and so on.

Logic: start from the widest apart. Each step, move the SHORTER wall, because the taller wall does not block. This way every step safely eliminates one wall, and you only need one pass.
